ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: Identifying individual wild animals helps the study of field ecology. In recent years, people have found that the animal's DNA can be extracted from animal feces, specific DNA fragments can be amplified by PCR, and the length or sequence of the product can be determined; based on this, individuals can be identified, and on this basis multiple kinds of ecological information about wild animals can be obtained. Microsatellite DNA is a DNA fragment commonly used for individual identification and is widely distributed in the nuclear genome. Each microsatellite DNA is a segment of tandem repeat sequence; the length of each repeat unit is 2~6bp (base pairs), and the number of repeats can reach dozens (Figure 1). There are many microsatellite DNAs in the genome, distributed at different positions. The microsatellite DNA at each position can be regarded as a "gene"; because the numbers of repeat units are different, the microsatellite "gene" at the same position can have multiple "alleles" and can form multiple "genotypes". Analyzing multiple microsatellite "genes" can obtain an individual-specific combination of "genotypes", thereby distinguishing different individuals. There is an isolated island far from the mainland, which terrestrial mammals can hardly reach, and human activities brought the carnivore raccoon dog to the island. Scientists collected fresh feces of raccoon dogs on the island, extracted DNA, amplified and analyzed 10 microsatellite "genes", and as a result successfully identified individuals in 30 samples (as in the table). Several months later, fresh feces of raccoon dogs were collected again, and the same analysis was carried out, successfully identifying individuals in 40 samples (as in the table). Based on this, please use the mark-recapture method to estimate what the population size of raccoon dogs on this island is?

ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The table is divided into two parts. The title of the upper part is "Individual numbers corresponding to the 30 fecal samples collected for the first time"; after deduplication, the visible individual numbers are N01 to N24, for a total of 24 individuals. The title of the lower part is "Individual numbers corresponding to the 40 fecal samples collected for the second time"; after deduplication, there are 32 individuals in total. The individual numbers appearing repeatedly in the two samplings are N03, N04, N05, N08, N09, N12, N14, N18, N23, N24, for a total of 10. Reasoning: According to the mark-recapture method, the number of individuals identified the first time is used as the number marked M=24, the number of individuals identified the second time is used as the number recaptured C=32, and the number of individuals common to both times is used as the number of recaptured marked individuals R=10. The estimated population size N≈M×C/R=24×32/10=76.8, rounded to about 77 individuals.
